newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Nov 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Nov 26.

text.p: The following is a summary of major South Korean political stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not gaurantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.
- South Korea, the United States agree to pursue four-way peace talks while trying to obtain North Korea's apology for a September submarine incursion.
- Manila Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum adopts manifesto calling for removal of tariffs on information and technology products.
- Share prices tumble to three-year low, with index plunging to 716.45 points, down 14.99 points from the previous day.
- Greenbelt deregulation draft plan mapped out by ruling New Korea party to erode about 1.8 billion square metres of protected green belt land over 10 years following the plan's implementation.

- South Korea-U.S. missile talks scheduled for early next month are expected to face rough going, according to a Korean government source. The U.S. side calls for a continued ban on South Korea's development of missiles with ranges of 300 km and for Seoul's guarantee for transparency in missile technology development.
- Leaders attending the APEC forum approved Manila action plan for free trade. President Kim Young-sam stressed the importance of the APEC education fund, promised $10 million as Korea's share.
- American congressman flies to Pyongyang to get release of American detainee, Carl Hunziker.
